- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 5–10% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent high or use 30-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently under-reacts; increase forecast by 3–5% relative to prior 7-day mean.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early 30d horizon — over-forecasting near 30-day high; apply downward correction of 2–5% if price > 30d high.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to lag true trend by 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending upward.
- If sentiment is consistently positive and price is trending upward, model often under-estimates upside; add 2–4% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.6 for 3+ consecutive days.
- Avoid extrapolating from 18-day history alone — sentiment over 10 days is more predictive than 18-day price history for 30d horizon.
